title: Virtual threads (Java 21) — do they make @Async, CompletableFuture, thread pools obsolete?

s1_definition.profdef: **Virtual threads** (Java 21, Project Loom) are lightweight threads managed by the JVM — NOT the OS. You can create MILLIONS of them (each ~1KB stack vs ~1MB for platform threads). They're mounted on a small pool of carrier (platform) threads. When a virtual thread blocks on IO (DB, HTTP, sleep), the JVM UNMOUNTS it from the carrier → carrier thread is free for another virtual thread. This means: simple `Thread.sleep()`, blocking `socket.read()`, JDBC queries — all become "non-blocking" under the hood without async code! **BUT**: virtual threads do NOT replace everything: (1) **CompletableFuture** still needed for composing/combining independent calls (`thenCombine`/`allOf`), timeouts, fallbacks. (2) **Bounded platform thread pools** still needed for CPU-bound parallelism (virtual threads don't speed up compute). (3) "Async is dead" is an overstatement.
s1_definition.analogy: **Platform threads** = full-time permanent tellers (expensive, limited to ~200). **Virtual threads** = freelance tellers on call (millions available, almost free). When a freelance teller waits for the vault (IO block), they STEP ASIDE and another freelance uses the counter (carrier thread). With virtual threads: write simple "one teller per customer" code → scales to 1M customers because tellers are free while waiting. BUT: for COUNTING CASH (CPU work), you still need permanent tellers at dedicated counters (platform thread pool). And for "fetch balance AND credit score simultaneously, combine results" → still need CompletableFuture's `thenCombine`.
s1_definition.oneliner: Virtual threads: millions of lightweight threads, blocking becomes non-blocking internally. Replaces @Async + thread pool tuning for IO. CF still needed for composition/combining. Platform pools still needed for CPU-bound. "Async is dead" = overstatement.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** **Virtual threads** (Java 21, Project Loom) are lightweight threads managed by the JVM — NOT the OS. You can create MILLIONS of them (each ~1KB stack vs ~1MB for platform threads). They're mounted on a small pool of carrier (platform) threads. When a virtual thread blocks on IO (DB, HTTP, sleep), the JVM UNMOUNTS it from the carrier → carrier thread is free for another virtual thread. This means: simple `Thread.sleep()`, blocking `socket.read()`, JDBC queries — all become "non-blocking" under the hood without async code! **BUT**: virtual threads do NOT replace everything: (1) **CompletableFuture** still needed for composing/combining independent calls (`thenCombine`/`allOf`), timeouts, fallbacks. (2) **Bounded platform thread pools** still needed for CPU-bound parallelism (virtual threads don't speed up compute). (3) "Async is dead" is an overstatement.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** **Platform threads** = full-time permanent tellers (expensive, limited to ~200). **Virtual threads** = freelance tellers on call (millions available, almost free). When a freelance teller waits for the vault (IO block), they STEP ASIDE and another freelance uses the counter (carrier thread). With virtual threads: write simple "one teller per customer" code → scales to 1M customers because tellers are free while waiting. BUT: for COUNTING CASH (CPU work), you still need permanent tellers at dedicated counters (platform thread pool). And for "fetch balance AND credit score simultaneously, combine results" → still need CompletableFuture's `thenCombine`.

**One line to remember:** Virtual threads: millions of lightweight threads, blocking becomes non-blocking internally. Replaces @Async + thread pool tuning for IO. CF still needed for composition/combining. Platform pools still needed for CPU-bound. "Async is dead" = overstatement.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The bank's API gateway handled 10K concurrent requests.** With platform threads: `newFixedThreadPool(200)` → max 200 concurrent. With @Async + CompletableFuture: complex async code, hard to debug. Fix (Java 21): `Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()` → one virtual thread per request → 10K concurrent with simple blocking code. `repository.findById()` blocks → virtual thread unmounted → carrier free. BUT: the loan approval pipeline still uses `CompletableFuture.allOf(creditScore, propertyValue, income)` because it COMBINES three parallel calls with `orTimeout(5s)`.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** 10K virtual threads created. Each: `Thread.sleep(100)` → JVM unmounts virtual thread from carrier → carrier thread serves another virtual thread.

**Step 2.** ~4 carrier threads serve 10K virtual threads by switching when blocking. All 10K complete in ~100-200ms. With platform threads: 10K × 1MB = 10GB → OOM!

**Step 3.** Loan approval: `CompletableFuture.allOf(creditScore, property, income).orTimeout(5s)` → three parallel calls combined with timeout. Virtual threads alone can't express this composition as cleanly.
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ VIRTUAL THREADS vs PLATFORM THREADS ═══

  Platform: 200 threads × 1MB = 200MB. Max 200 concurrent.
  Virtual:  10K threads × 1KB = 10MB.  10K concurrent!

  ═══ WHAT REPLACES WHAT ═══

  @Async + pool tuning for IO:     → virtual threads (Recommended) (simpler!)
  CompletableFuture composition:    → CF still needed (Recommended) (allOf, thenCombine)
  Platform pool for CPU-bound:      → still needed (Recommended) (parallelStream)
  "Async is dead":                  → OVERSTATEMENT!

  ═══ VIRTUAL THREAD MOUNTING ═══

  Virtual Thread-1: run → IO block → UNMOUNT from Carrier-1
  Carrier-1: FREE → picks Virtual Thread-2 → runs it
  Virtual Thread-1: IO done → MOUNT on Carrier-2 → continues
  4 carriers serve 10,000 virtual threads!
```

sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — Virtual Thread Internals ═══

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Virtual Thread                       │
  │  - stack: ~1KB (grows on demand)     │  vs 1MB platform
  │  - carrier: platform thread (or null)│
  │  - continuation: saved state         │
  │  + isVirtual(): true                 │
  │  Lifecycle: mount → run → IO block → │
  │    unmount → carrier free → IO done → │
  │    remount (maybe different carrier)  │
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Carrier (Platform Thread)            │
  │  ForkJoinPool (cores threads)         │
  │  Serves 1000s of virtual threads     │
  │  by switching on IO block!            │
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘

  ═══ WHEN TO USE WHAT ═══
  IO fan-out (10K DB calls):  virtual threads (blocking code, simple!)
  Compose parallel calls:     CompletableFuture (allOf, thenCombine)
  Timeouts/fallbacks:         CompletableFuture (orTimeout, exceptionally)
  CPU parallelism:            platform thread pool (parallelStream)
  Structured concurrency:     StructuredTaskScope (Java 21 preview)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Virtual threads (Java 21) are lightweight JVM-managed threads — millions possible (~1KB stack each). When a virtual thread blocks on IO, the JVM unmounts it from the carrier thread → carrier serves another virtual thread. This means simple blocking code (`repository.findById()`, `httpClient.send()`) scales to 10K+ concurrent requests without async complexity. Virtual threads REPLACE: `@Async` annotations, custom thread pool tuning for IO-bound work, and simple `CompletableFuture.supplyAsync()` wrapping.

But "async is dead" is an overstatement. CompletableFuture is STILL needed for: composing independent parallel calls (`thenCombine`/`allOf`), timeouts (`orTimeout`), fallbacks (`exceptionally`), and pipeline transformations. Platform thread pools are STILL needed for CPU-bound parallelism — virtual threads don't speed up computation (they share the same carrier pool = cores threads). In banking: API gateway → virtual threads (10K concurrent IO). Loan approval combining 3 parallel checks → CompletableFuture. Encryption batch → platform thread pool. Each tool has its place.

---

keyPoints: Virtual threads: cheap, blocking IO is fine
CF still useful for composition, fan-out, timeouts
